It was played at [[Beşiktaş Stadium]] in [[Istanbul]], Turkey, on 20 May 2026 between German club [[SC Freiburg]] and English club [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. Aston Villa won the match 3–0 for their first UEFA Europa League title, their second European title after winning the [[1982 European Cup final]] and their first overall title since winning the [[1996 Football League Cup final]].{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/02a5-20ac3759bba4-7f91e47690b9-1000/ |title=Freiburg 0–3 Aston Villa: Rampant Villans win Europa League for the first time |publisher=UEFA |date=20 May 2026 |access-date=20 May 2026}} As winners, they earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]], [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], in the [[2026 UEFA Super Cup]]. Since Aston Villa had already qualified to enter the league phase of the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League]] through their league performance, the league phase spot reserved for the Europa League title holders was vacated and the access list was rebalanced. ==Background== Freiburg reached their first ever European final. They were aiming for a first major title. Freiburg's previous best European run was reaching the Europa League round of 16 twice, in [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League#Round of 16|2022–23]] and [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League#Round of 16|2023–24]]. Aston Villa reached their first UEFA Cup/Europa League final and a third European final, having won the [[1982 European Cup final]] and [[1982 European Super Cup]]. They were seeking a first major trophy since winning the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] in [[1995–96 Football League Cup|1996]], thus discounting them being one of the three winners of the [[2001 UEFA Intertoto Cup]]. This was their best [[Aston Villa F.C. in international football|European run]] across three successive seasons after a 13-year absence, having lost the semi-finals of the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League]] to eventual winners [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] before elimination in the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League]] quarter-finals to another eventual winner in [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]]. Their previous furthest run in the UEFA Cup/Europa League was the quarter-finals in [[1977–78 UEFA Cup|1977–78]] and [[1997–98 UEFA Cup|1997–98]]. Villa head coach [[Unai Emery]] was looking for a record-extending [[List of UEFA Cup and Europa League–winning managers|fifth]] UEFA Cup/Europa League title and the first with a non-Spanish side, having won three with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] ([[2014 UEFA Europa League final|2014]], [[2015 UEFA Europa League final|2015]], [[2016 UEFA Europa League final|2016]]) and one with [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] ([[2021 UEFA Europa League final|2021]]) sandwiching his defeat with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2019]]. Their striker [[Tammy Abraham]] was aiming to become the 11th player to have [[UEFA club competition records and statistics#List of players to have won the three main European club competitions|won all three major European trophies]] and the first to have achieved that with three different clubs, having won the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]] with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League]] with [[AS Roma|Roma]]. ===Previous finals=== ''In the following table, finals until 2009 were in the UEFA Cup era and since 2010 were in the UEFA Europa League era.'' {| class="wikitable" |- !Team !Previous final appearance (Bold indicates winners) |- | {{#invoke:flag|fbaicon|Germany}} [[SC Freiburg]] | none |- | {{#invoke:flag|fbaicon|England}} [[Aston Villa]] | none |} ==Venue== [[File:20220606-L1000240.jpg|thumb|[[Beşiktaş Stadium]] in [[Istanbul]] hosted the final.]] ===Host selection=== On 17 May 2023, UEFA opened the bidding process for the final, which was held in parallel with that of the [[2027 UEFA Europa League final|2027 final]]. Interested bidders could bid for either one or both of the finals. Additionally, bidding associations could only be appointed one UEFA final in a given year. The proposed venues had to include natural grass and be ranked as a [[UEFA stadium categories|UEFA category four stadium]], with a gross capacity of 40,000 to 60,000 preferred.
